content:
sofia: Heads up — during last night's autoscaler burst we observed a spike of GPU pod restarts/bouncing across nodes when traffic shifted eu-west1 -> us-west1. Symptoms: pods failing readiness and getting evicted, kube-proxy logs with conntrack errors, and network flaps. Anyone triaging?

sam: saw it in the metrics alert feed. conntrack entries jumped quickly on several nodes around 01:14 UTC, approaching the system limit. Pods didn’t have high CPU, just network churn. :eyes:

mike: pulling diagnostics now. pasted `conntrack -S` snapshot below.

mike: ```
# conntrack -S
Entries: 248732
Found: 248732
Invalid: 12
Expectations: 0

# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
262144

# kubectl -n gpu logs kube-proxy-node-abc -c kube-proxy | tail -n50
E0321 01:15:09.123 kube-proxy: conntrack: nf_conntrack overflow, new entries dropped
E0321 01:15:09.125 kube-proxy: service sync failed, will retry
```

jun: interesting — overflow + kube-proxy retry usually causes ephemeral load balancing mismatches (packets dropped or mis-routed). If healthchecks fail, kubelet kills pods -> scheduler reschedules -> repeat. That explains the bounce.

nora: autoscaler landed ~20 extra nodes in eu-west1, but a subset of queued jobs were routed to us-west1 due to resource pressure. Cross-region flows increased NAT table usage on egress nodes (we have SNAT gateways). Didn’t have conntrack tuning in the egress path.

sam: right. The traffic pattern was many short-lived connections to external artifact buckets from init containers. Lots of 1-2 second TCP flows -> conntrack churn.

sofia: rough impact: ~150 pod restarts across the pool over 20 minutes, higher latencies for our internal RPCs, and a small bump in cost because of reschedules.

mike: quick fixes on a few nodes: bump nf_conntrack_max and tune timeouts to reduce ephemeral entries. Commands we ran:

mike: ```sh
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
echo 524288 | sudo tee /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
# reduce tcp timeout to avoid long-lived half-open entries (example)
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300
```

jun: medium term: we should harden kube-proxy conntrack settings, and add guards in the autoscaler to avoid cross-region spillback for short-lived init-heavy jobs. Also consider enabling conntrack hashing and per-node limits.

nora: action items proposal: 1) Immediate cluster-wide bump for nf_conntrack_max via daemonset (safe rollback) 2) Add a prefilter to the autoscaler to avoid routing bursty init jobs cross-region 3) Add a temporary alert for conntrack_entries > 80% with playbook to cordon nodes and rollout conntrack bump 4) Investigate moving artifact pulls to regional caches so we don't hit SNAT egress as much.

sofia: +1 to the plan. Can infra team own (1) and (3) today? We can pair with platform to update autoscaler rules (2) tomorrow.

sam: I'll open a short PR for daemonset sysctl with a readiness probe so we don’t regress. tagging @jun for autoscaler rule change.

jun: ack, will prototype autoscaler filter and add a test simulating many short TCP flows.

infra-bot: deploy-status: daemonset/conntrack-bump started rollout in eu-west1 (3/60 pods ready)

mike: monitoring note: after bump we saw conntrack entries stabilize ~120k and no more kube-proxy overflow logs. Pods stopped bouncing within ~6m of rollout.

nora: logging follow-up: capturing a handful of pcap + conntrack dumps for the incident runbook. Will attach to the incident ticket.

sofia: Thanks everyone — please add any follow-ups to the incident ticket and let's schedule a short retro for tuning autoscaler vs cross-region flows. :thumbsup:
